title: Orchestra routing graph

schema.route_fields: if (prose predicate) · then (string step, or array = parallel batch) · dispatch (tokens role[:lens][@level], resolvable against roles; @L2 default) · next (forward edge, must name a real state) · back_to + carry (backward edge + what travels back)
schema.state_fields: question · always (duties that fire on every entry, before route matching) · routes · match ('first' default = exclusive; 'all' = every matching route fires, at most one names next)
schema.announce: Every transition is announced in chat as `flow: <from> -> <to> (<matched if>)`. A transition without an announcement is a routing defect.
schema.validate: python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.cursor/skills/orchestrator/flow.json'));s=set(d['states']);bad=[(k,e) for k,v in d['states'].items() for r in v.get('routes',[]) for e in [r.get('next'),r.get('back_to')] if e and e not in s];print(bad or 'edges ok')"
schema.reentry: A back_to carry OVERRIDES the target state's entry route text and stays active until the re-entered loop completes (e.g. plan.redteam re-entry after repair re-dispatches only the repaired lens; execute.ticket-loop re-entry on findings resumes the SAME builder; gates.fast re-entry after gate-repair skips execute.wave-close's always batch).

roles.orchestrator: main session — talks to the user, dispatches everyone, adjudicates, merges, approves, owns memory

levels: Dispatch tokens carry @L1 (minimal) / @L2 (standard, default) / @L3 (deep). Each agent file defines what its levels mean — the level contract travels in the brief. Which roles fire in which state, and at what level, IS the activation model; there is no separate matrix.

state_files.docs/orchestra/STATE.md: working memory — orchestrator sole writer; pointers not content; rewritten at wave/batch closes and before deliberate stops; stamped `written-at: <timestamp> @ <git HEAD>`; working-tree file, committed only inside batch-closing commits; 120-line cap is a smoke alarm (over = you are duplicating content that has a home), never an eviction trigger; verbatim quotes only when a ruling fits one line, else pointer only — never a trimmed quote
state_files..orchestra/state.json: machine run-record (gitignored) — exact keys: gates.last_green_hash (the green commit hash; the hook denies protected pushes while it differs from HEAD), gates.reports{<hash>: report}, redteam{verdicts,rounds,run_ids}, reviews{<ticket>: verdict, pr: CLEAN|BLOCKED}, flakes[], subagent_state_path. Written by the orchestrator at the transitions marked here; read by hooks and the janitor.
state_files.docs/plans/<feature>-ledger.md: run state for one plan — always a separate file, never a section in the plan; CLOSED stamp at archive
state_files.docs/AGENT-MEMORY.md: long-term repo memory — fill-in index (how-to-fill + Current); janitor drafts and prunes, orchestrator commits in the batch-closing commit; git is the history — no append-only markers
state_files..orchestra/delivery.json: per-repo delivery declaration (COMMITTED, unlike gitignored .orchestra/ files): provider (github | azure-devops | gitlab | plain-git), protected_branches, landing (pr | direct), server_side_gate (host enforces the gate itself), deploy policy per environment (default auto), deploy_commands patterns the hook allows only with CLEAN+fresh. install.sh detects the provider from the remote URL; the orchestrator reads this file before any release action.
state_files..orchestra/package-version: install stamp (COMMITTED via gitignore exception): copy of repo-root VERSION plus git describe. Written by install.sh so a host can see which orchestra package it merged.

always: If the request names multiple independent features, open one plan per feature and run every non-colliding current wave together. Do not serialize independent features.

design.spec.question: Is the spec drafted?

routes.if: 3+ rulings or more than one approach explored
routes.then: architect drafts the spec from recon + winning approach + verbatim rulings; diff its returned Rulings section against your record — any difference is a defect

always: Terms ruled on this phase are written to CONTEXT.md (glossary only). Seams the tests will assert at are named in the spec — the plan inherits them.
Name seams and module boundaries so the planner can cut tracer-bullet tickets that run in parallel. A spec that forces a single serial builder when the surface is independent is unfinished.

always: Do not wait for a user OK. The original request plus any frontier answers are the rulings. Red-team spot-check is the spec gate.

always: Version-sensitive claims cite RESEARCH.md on disk — a ticket depending on research that does not exist yet is BLOCKED-ON-RESEARCH, not guessed.

Segment for maximum safe parallelism: exclusive file lists, wave map, blocking edges only where files or data truly collide. Independent tickets share a wave. Independent features are separate plans whose current waves may run in the same dispatch batch. Serial is a recorded exception, not the default.

execute.setup.question: How many builders edit concurrently, and do they share a filesystem?
always: Ledger file (docs/plans/<feature>-ledger.md) exists before the first dispatch.
Never git stash while worktrees exist.

Maximize parallelism without mixing work: dispatch every unblocked ticket in the current wave whose files do not overlap, in one message. Serial only on a blocking edge, shared file ownership, or a failed worktree proof. You hire N builders; a builder never hires another builder.

routes.then: main tree, no worktree

routes.if: 2+ builders sharing one checkout (local session, or sub-agents inside ONE cloud VM)
routes.then: one worktree per builder (git worktree add <repo>/.cursor/worktrees/<ticket> -b <ticket-branch>; check you are not already inside one; .cursor/worktrees/ gitignored); install dependencies and PROVE each toolchain before dispatch; own ports per tree. Cursor 3.5+ may delete unmanaged worktree dirs (~/.cursor/worktrees/, cursor.worktreeMaxCount); named-branch commits are the preservation. Ledger git_branch from subagentStart (nest hook records it). Janitor inspects git worktree list, not only .cursor/worktrees/<ticket>.

routes.if: each builder is its own cloud agent (separate VM and clone)
routes.then: no worktrees — the VM is the isolation; each pushes its own branch, and integration happens by fetching those branches; anything the next role needs must be COMMITTED, since gitignored files do not travel

routes.if: yes (several independent → parallel, worktree rule applies)

Widening is mechanical, not judgment: a diff touching dependency manifests, build/tsconfig, migrations/schema, shared types/tokens, or auth widens the scoped set.

Record the verdict in the ledger and .orchestra/state.json as reviews.pr = CLEAN or BLOCKED (plus worst severity). That reviews.pr = CLEAN key is what the shell hook reads as merge authorization. Nits/Trivial never block merge. This does not replace the gatekeeper or the per-ticket reviewer.

release.merge.question: Who gates the merge — the host (server_side_gate) or the local hash record — and can the gated hash be the shipped hash?
always: Read the repo's delivery declaration (AGENTS.md 'Delivery' slot + .orchestra/delivery.json): provider, protected branches, landing rule, server_side_gate, deploy policy. Use that provider's CLI (github: gh · azure-devops: az repos · gitlab: glab · plain-git: git). server_side_gate is true only when a host branch policy actually runs the fast set — do not infer it from an Azure remote URL alone.

Hook floor: force-push/stash/rebase/hard-reset are deny. The hook never returns ask (no human click). pr-reviewer CLEAN + matching last_green_hash allows land and declared deploys, including headless. Without that pair, protected landings and declared deploys are deny. server_side_gate allows host-mediated PR completion. Full e2e is never a merge precondition.

routes.if: server_side_gate true (e.g. Azure DevOps branch policy with build validation)
routes.then: make sure the host's required checks match the fast set; mark the PR ready and set auto-complete — the platform gates and merges the preview merge commit, so the gated hash is provably the shipped hash

routes.if: no server-side gate, fast-gate green at HEAD, branch current with the target
routes.then: mark the PR ready with the final gate report; merge fast-forward so the gated hash becomes the target HEAD

routes.if: no server-side gate and the branch is behind the target

routes.if: merge done and no deploy is configured or in scope for this change

routes.if: health check fails, or main breaks after merge

routes.then: releaser stages the revert of the merge commit; execute; verify the health check at the reverted state

autonomy.loop.question: Unattended mode: is there an unfinished ledger item and budget left?
always: A ledger file (docs/plans/<feature>-ledger.md, or the path STATE.md points at) must exist; otherwise NOT-READY — autonomy cannot start without a plan.
Cursor may merge. A host block-pr-merge.sh rail is a defect — install.sh strips it. After pr-reviewer CLEAN the releaser lands and deploys; do not wait for a human.
Never invent work: the loop only advances items already in the plan's ledger. Extra ideas go to the polish queue — do not stop for the user.
Each pass is a fresh dispatch through the normal chain (execute.ticket-loop → execute.review → gates.fast); autonomy changes WHO decides to continue, never WHAT the roles do.
A ledger item flips to done only on evidence (command + exit code). Flipping without evidence is the one tamper rule.

routes.then: NOT-READY — leave this state; autonomy cannot start without a plan

record caps (user-stated or defaults: max passes 20, consecutive no-progress 2). After pr-reviewer CLEAN, releaser lands and deploys — that CLEAN is authorization, not a second chat OK. Do not halt for deploy. Full e2e is never in this loop. Announce the caps on the first pass.

routes.if: an unblocked ledger item remains and caps are not hit
routes.then: run one pass through the normal chain, record the result, loop

routes.if: two consecutive passes produce no new completed item, or the same failure signature repeats
routes.then: STALLED — stop and report; a loop that is not converging burns budget without learning

routes.if: a pass needs a land or deploy action
routes.then: releaser executes it after pr-reviewer CLEAN; do not halt for a chat OK. Destructive git stays deny. Host MCP apply_migration stays denied if that rail exists.

routes.if: a finding contradicts the plan or spec, or new scope appears
routes.then: orchestrator adjudicates: original request wins; park extras on the polish queue; do not stop unless a frontier decision the request never settled appears
EXHAUSTED — report what completed, what remains, and the next action

user changes a ruling mid-run.then: record the resume point (ledger + STATE.md); settle in-flight dispatches per the ledger; architect L1 revision of the spec carrying the new ruling verbatim -> design.gate (spot-check, no user OK); then planner Repair scoped to the affected tickets only -> plan.redteam re-dispatching ONLY the touched lenses; then re-enter execute.ticket-loop at the recorded resume point
user changes a ruling mid-run.carry: the new ruling verbatim + the recorded resume point

user interrupt during execution.then: stop dispatching; report ledger state; resume from the ledger — never re-dispatch blind (two builders on one ticket in one tree is corruption)

a dispatch errors or never returns.then: check the ledger and tree for partial commits, then dispatch fresh; liveness for background agents = state file + mtime at the verified sub-agent state path

invariants: Sub-agent briefs are self-contained: verbatim-critical excerpts (rulings, done_when, path rules) pasted; bulk material passed as pointers the agent reads itself.

Sub-agents never spawn sub-agents, including more of their own role (policy; subagentStart hook denies it). All fan-out is the orchestrator's: N concurrent instances of one role per wave, as the plan names.
User rulings travel verbatim — full quote only when it fits one line, else pointer; never a trimmed quote.
Evidence = command + exit code (captured without pipes) or both-theme screenshots; assertions are not evidence.
Worktrees only for 2+ concurrent editors; created, integrated, and removed by the orchestrator within the wave.
Judgement roles (architect, planner, red-teamer, auditor, builder-max, pr-reviewer) run model: inherit — the ceiling; the rest are pinned lower at install (install.sh verifies).

Approval boundaries: destructive git is deny. The hook never returns ask. pr-reviewer CLEAN + matching last_green_hash is merge and deploy authorization (including headless). Without CLEAN, protected landings and declared deploys are deny. The only user-facing stop after intake is design.frontier for decisions the request did not settle. Specs, plans, reviews, merges, and deploys do not wait. Full e2e is never in the execute/review/release chain.
Memory lands in the batch-closing commit; stale entries are pruned, not superseded-in-place.
Honest terminal states — DONE, BLOCKED, NOT-READY, NEEDS-APPROVAL; never one dressed as another.

cloud.topology: DEFAULT (A): one cloud agent IS the orchestrator; its sub-agents are children inside that same VM, sharing one clone. Everything in this graph applies unchanged. ALTERNATIVE (B): one cloud agent per independent FEATURE or ticket, each running its own mini-chain and returning a PR. Never split ROLES across VMs — roles are coupled by handoffs, and every boundary would become a git round-trip.
cloud.worktrees: Topology A: sub-agents share the VM's single clone and single git index, so the local rule applies unchanged — 2+ concurrent builders get worktrees inside the VM. Topology B: each VM is already an isolated clone; no worktrees.
cloud.handoff: Topology A: briefs + shared disk, as local. Topology B: nothing but git (pushed branches) and the orchestrator relaying report text — anything load-bearing must be committed, because gitignored files do not exist in a fresh clone.
cloud.conversation: A cloud orchestrator cannot hold a live conversation; it reaches the user asynchronously (Slack, web, PR comments). Design and plan are conversations — run them locally. Execute waves are the natural cloud workload.
cloud.enforcement: The hook never returns ask. Headless land/deploy is allow when reviews.pr=CLEAN and gates.last_green_hash matches HEAD (write those in-session before the releaser). A fresh clone has no state.json — seed from docs/orchestra/state.example.json; a protected landing with no CLEAN+fresh record is DENIED. server_side_gate allows host-mediated PR completion. Hooks also do not run during a cloud agent's early read-only turns.
cloud.config: Repo-level config travels with the clone (.cursor/agents, .cursor/skills, .cursor/hooks.json, AGENTS.md). User-level config (~/.cursor/*) does NOT. Keep this package project-scoped.
